完成权威来源替换、章节级证据、canonical 去重、全节点与先修边人工批准。

nodes.name: SI Base Units
nodes.description: The seven SI base units from which all other units are derived, used to express physical quantities consistently in measurement and calculation.

nodes.name: Homogeneity of Equations
nodes.description: Checking the homogeneity of an equation by ensuring both sides have the same base units, a test of its dimensional consistency.

nodes.name: Scalars and Vectors
nodes.description: The distinction between scalar quantities having only magnitude and vector quantities having both magnitude and direction, with vector addition and resolution.

nodes.name: Errors and Uncertainties
nodes.description: Systematic and random errors in measurement, and expressing the uncertainty of a reading as an absolute, fractional, or percentage uncertainty.

nodes.name: Combining Uncertainties
nodes.description: Combining uncertainties through calculations by adding absolute uncertainties for sums and fractional uncertainties for products and powers.

nodes.name: Displacement Velocity Acceleration
nodes.description: Displacement, velocity, and acceleration as related vector quantities describing motion, defined through rates of change of position.

nodes.name: Equations of Motion
nodes.description: The equations of motion for uniform acceleration relating displacement, initial and final velocity, acceleration, and time.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate uniform-acceleration motion with adjustable acceleration and initial velocity.

nodes.name: Motion Graphs
nodes.description: Interpreting displacement-time and velocity-time graphs, where gradients give velocity and acceleration and areas give displacement.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot displacement-time and velocity-time graphs, relating gradients and areas.

nodes.name: Free Fall
nodes.description: Motion under gravity alone with constant acceleration g, including the experimental determination of the acceleration of free fall.
nodes.visual_hint: Drop an object under gravity showing constant acceleration g.

nodes.name: Projectile Motion
nodes.description: Projectile motion analysed by treating the horizontal and vertical components independently under constant gravitational acceleration.
nodes.visual_hint: Launch a projectile with sliders for speed and angle showing the parabolic path.

nodes.name: Newton's Laws of Motion
nodes.description: Newton's three laws of motion relating force, mass, and acceleration and describing action-reaction force pairs.
nodes.visual_hint: Apply a force to a mass and watch the resulting acceleration.

nodes.name: Mass and Weight
nodes.description: The distinction between mass as the amount of matter and weight as the gravitational force on a mass, related by the field strength g.

nodes.name: Drag and Terminal Velocity
nodes.description: For motion with drag that increases with speed, the acceleration falls as the resultant force decreases; terminal velocity is reached when drag balances the driving force so resultant force and acceleration are zero.
nodes.visual_hint: Vary drag and weight to show acceleration approaching zero at terminal velocity.

nodes.name: Linear Momentum
nodes.description: Linear momentum as the product of mass and velocity, a vector quantity central to analysing motion and collisions.

nodes.name: Conservation of Momentum
nodes.description: The principle of conservation of momentum, where total momentum is conserved in a closed system with no external resultant force.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate a collision conserving total momentum.

nodes.name: Impulse and Collisions
nodes.description: Impulse as the product of force and time, equal to the change in momentum, applied to analyse elastic and inelastic collisions.

nodes.name: Types of Force
nodes.description: The types of force acting on bodies, including gravitational, normal contact, friction, tension, and upthrust forces.

nodes.name: Centre of Gravity
nodes.description: The centre of gravity is the single point through which an object's whole weight may be considered to act, used when analysing equilibrium, stability and moments due to weight.

nodes.name: Moments and Couples
nodes.description: The moment of a force as force times perpendicular distance, and couples producing rotation, with the principle of moments for equilibrium.
nodes.visual_hint: Balance a beam by adjusting forces and distances (moments).

nodes.name: Equilibrium of Forces
nodes.description: The conditions for equilibrium, where both the resultant force and the resultant moment acting on a body are zero.

nodes.name: Density and Pressure
nodes.description: Density as mass per unit volume and pressure as force per unit area, including the variation of pressure with depth in a fluid.

nodes.name: Upthrust and Archimedes
nodes.description: Upthrust as the buoyant force on a body in a fluid, equal by Archimedes' principle to the weight of fluid displaced.
nodes.visual_hint: Float or sink an object showing upthrust versus weight.

nodes.name: Work Done
nodes.description: Work done as the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force, transferring energy to or from a system.

nodes.name: Kinetic and Potential Energy
nodes.description: Kinetic energy of a moving body and gravitational potential energy due to position, with their defining formulae.

nodes.name: Conservation of Energy
nodes.description: The principle of conservation of energy, where energy is transferred between forms but the total amount remains constant.

nodes.name: Power and Efficiency
nodes.description: Power as the rate of doing work or transferring energy, and efficiency as the ratio of useful output to total input energy.

nodes.name: Hooke's Law
nodes.description: Hooke's law stating that the extension of a spring is proportional to the applied force up to the limit of proportionality.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot force against extension for a spring with a slider for stiffness.

nodes.name: Stress, Strain and Young Modulus
nodes.description: Tensile stress as force per unit area and strain as fractional extension, related by the Young modulus for an elastic material.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot a stress-strain curve up to fracture.

nodes.name: Elastic and Plastic Behaviour
nodes.description: Elastic behaviour where a material returns to its original shape and plastic behaviour where deformation is permanent beyond the elastic limit.

nodes.name: Elastic Strain Energy
nodes.description: Elastic strain energy stored in a deformed material, equal to the area under its force-extension graph.

nodes.name: Progressive Waves
nodes.description: Progressive waves transferring energy through a medium, described by displacement, amplitude, wavelength, frequency, and speed.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate a progressive wave with sliders for amplitude, wavelength, and frequency.

nodes.name: Transverse and Longitudinal Waves
nodes.description: The distinction between transverse waves oscillating perpendicular to the direction of travel and longitudinal waves oscillating parallel to it.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate transverse versus longitudinal wave oscillation.

nodes.name: Wave Intensity
nodes.description: Wave intensity as power per unit area, proportional to the square of the amplitude and decreasing with distance from the source.

nodes.name: Electromagnetic Spectrum
nodes.description: The electromagnetic spectrum of transverse waves travelling at the speed of light, ranging from radio waves to gamma rays.
nodes.visual_hint: Labelled electromagnetic spectrum ordered by wavelength and frequency.

nodes.name: Polarisation and Malus's Law
nodes.description: Polarisation is a property of transverse waves; for plane-polarised electromagnetic radiation passing through an analyser, the transmitted intensity is calculated using I = I0 cos²θ.
nodes.visual_hint: Rotate an analyser and plot transmitted intensity according to Malus's law.

nodes.name: Doppler Effect
nodes.description: The Doppler effect, the change in observed frequency when a wave source and observer move relative to one another.
nodes.visual_hint: Move a wave source and show the observed frequency shift (Doppler effect).

nodes.name: Principle of Superposition
nodes.description: The principle of superposition stating that when waves meet, the resultant displacement is the vector sum of the individual displacements.

nodes.name: Two-Source Interference
nodes.description: Two-source interference producing constructive and destructive fringes where coherent waves meet in phase and out of phase.
nodes.visual_hint: Two-source interference producing constructive and destructive fringes.

nodes.name: Diffraction
nodes.description: The spreading of waves passing through a gap or around an obstacle, most pronounced when the gap is comparable to the wavelength.

nodes.name: Diffraction Grating
nodes.description: A diffraction grating producing sharp maxima at angles given by the grating equation, used to measure wavelength accurately.

nodes.name: Stationary Waves
nodes.description: Stationary waves formed by superposition of two opposite progressive waves, with fixed nodes and antinodes and no net energy transfer.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate a standing wave with nodes and antinodes; slider for the harmonic.

nodes.name: Electric Current and Charge
nodes.description: Electric current as the rate of flow of charge, with charge quantised in units of the elementary charge carried by electrons.

nodes.name: Potential Difference and EMF
nodes.description: Potential difference as energy transferred per unit charge by a component and electromotive force as energy supplied per unit charge by a source.

nodes.name: Resistance and Ohm's Law
nodes.description: Resistance as the ratio of potential difference to current, with Ohm's law holding when resistance is constant at fixed temperature.

nodes.name: Resistivity
nodes.description: Resistivity as a material property relating a conductor's resistance to its length and cross-sectional area.

nodes.name: Kirchhoff's Laws
nodes.description: Kirchhoff's first and second laws expressing the conservation of charge at junctions and of energy around circuit loops.
nodes.visual_hint: Circuit diagram applying Kirchhoff's current and voltage laws.

nodes.name: Series and Parallel Resistors
nodes.description: Combining resistors in series and parallel using the total-resistance rules derived from Kirchhoff's laws.
nodes.visual_hint: Build series and parallel resistor networks and compute total resistance.

nodes.name: I-V Characteristics
nodes.description: Current-voltage characteristics of components such as resistors, filament lamps, and diodes, revealing their electrical behaviour.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot I-V characteristics for a resistor, filament lamp, and diode.

nodes.name: Resistive Sensors
nodes.description: The resistance of an LDR decreases as light intensity increases, while the resistance of a negative-temperature-coefficient thermistor decreases as temperature increases; both can be used in sensing potential-divider circuits.
nodes.visual_hint: Compare LDR and NTC resistance curves and their effect on divider output voltage.

nodes.name: Potential Dividers
nodes.description: A potential divider using resistors in series to produce a desired fraction of the supply voltage, including with sensors.
nodes.visual_hint: Slider on a potential divider showing the output voltage.

nodes.name: Potentiometer and Null Methods
nodes.description: A potentiometer compares potential differences by using a galvanometer zero reading to identify balance, so no current is drawn from the measured source at the null point.

nodes.name: Internal Resistance
nodes.description: The internal resistance of a source causing the terminal potential difference to fall below the EMF when current flows.

nodes.name: Radian Measure and Angular Speed
nodes.description: Angular displacement in radians and angular speed as the rate of change of angle, related to linear speed by the radius.

nodes.name: Centripetal Acceleration
nodes.description: Centripetal acceleration directed toward the centre of a circular path, with magnitude expressed in terms of speed and radius.

nodes.name: Centripetal Force
nodes.description: The resultant centripetal force required for circular motion, directed toward the centre and provided by a real force.
nodes.visual_hint: Swing a mass in a circle, varying speed and radius for centripetal force.

nodes.name: Newton's Law of Gravitation
nodes.description: Newton's law of gravitation stating the attractive force between two point masses is proportional to their product and inversely to distance squared.

nodes.name: Gravitational Field Strength
nodes.description: Gravitational field strength as the gravitational force per unit mass at a point, a vector directed toward the mass.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot gravitational field strength against distance (inverse square).

nodes.name: Gravitational Potential
nodes.description: Gravitational potential as the work done per unit mass to bring a mass from infinity to a point, always negative.

nodes.name: Orbital Motion
nodes.description: Orbital motion where gravitation provides the centripetal force, relating orbital speed, radius, and period as in Kepler's third law.
nodes.visual_hint: Orbit a satellite where gravity provides the centripetal force.

nodes.name: Simple Harmonic Motion
nodes.description: Simple harmonic motion where acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed toward equilibrium, producing sinusoidal motion.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate a pendulum or spring in simple harmonic motion and plot displacement.

nodes.name: SHM Energy
nodes.description: The interchange between kinetic and potential energy in simple harmonic motion, with total energy constant in the absence of damping.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot the kinetic and potential energy interchange in SHM.

nodes.name: Damping
nodes.description: Damping reducing the amplitude of oscillations through energy loss, classified as light, critical, or heavy damping.

nodes.name: Resonance
nodes.description: Resonance where a system driven at its natural frequency oscillates with maximum amplitude, with damping reducing the peak.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot amplitude against driving frequency showing a resonance peak.

nodes.name: Temperature and Thermal Equilibrium
nodes.description: Temperature as a measure of the average kinetic energy of particles, with thermal equilibrium reached when no net heat flows.

nodes.name: Thermometry and the Thermodynamic Scale
nodes.description: Temperature can be measured using a physical property that varies monotonically, such as liquid density, constant-pressure gas volume, metal resistance or thermocouple e.m.f.; the thermodynamic temperature scale is independent of any particular material property.

nodes.name: Specific Heat and Latent Heat
nodes.description: Specific heat capacity for raising temperature and specific latent heat for changes of state, relating energy to mass and temperature.

nodes.name: Mole and Avogadro Constant
nodes.name_zh: 摩尔与阿伏伽德罗常数
nodes.description: One mole contains the Avogadro constant number of specified particles, linking amount of substance n to particle number N through N = nNA.

nodes.name: Kinetic Theory of Gases
nodes.description: The kinetic theory modelling a gas as many small particles in random motion, relating pressure to their mean square speed.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate gas particles in random motion inside a box.

nodes.name: Ideal Gas Law
nodes.description: The ideal-gas equations pV = nRT and pV = NkT, relating pressure, volume, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance and particle number, with k = R/NA connecting the Boltzmann, molar gas and Avogadro constants.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot pV = nRT relationships between pressure, volume, and temperature.

nodes.name: Internal Energy and First Law
nodes.description: Internal energy as the sum of the random kinetic and potential energies of particles, and the first law relating it to heat and work.

nodes.name: Coulomb's Law
nodes.description: Coulomb's law giving the electrostatic force between two point charges as proportional to their product and inversely to distance squared.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot the Coulomb force against separation (inverse square).

nodes.name: Electric Field Strength
nodes.description: Electric field strength as the force per unit positive charge at a point, a vector quantity directed along the field.
nodes.visual_hint: Show electric field lines around point charges.

nodes.name: Electric Potential
nodes.description: Electric potential as the work done per unit positive charge to bring a charge from infinity to a point in the field.

nodes.name: Gravitational and Electric Field Analogy
nodes.description: The analogy between gravitational and electric fields in their inverse-square laws, field strength, and potential, noting key differences.

nodes.name: Capacitance
nodes.description: Capacitance as the charge stored per unit potential difference, a measure of a capacitor's ability to store charge.

nodes.name: Capacitors in Series and Parallel
nodes.description: Combining capacitors in series and parallel using the total-capacitance rules, which are opposite to those for resistors.

nodes.name: Energy Stored in a Capacitor
nodes.description: The energy stored in a charged capacitor, equal to the area under its charge-voltage graph.

nodes.name: Charging and Discharging
nodes.description: The exponential charging and discharging of a capacitor through a resistor, characterised by the time constant RC.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot exponential capacitor charge and discharge against time.

nodes.name: Magnetic Flux Density
nodes.description: Magnetic flux density as a measure of the strength of a magnetic field, defined through the force on a current-carrying conductor.

nodes.name: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor
nodes.description: The force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, given by F equals BIL, with direction from Fleming's left-hand rule.
nodes.visual_hint: Show the motor-effect force on a current-carrying conductor (Fleming's left hand).

nodes.name: Force on a Moving Charge
nodes.description: The force on a charge moving through a magnetic field, given by F equals Bqv, causing charged particles to follow circular paths.

nodes.name: Hall Effect and Hall Voltage
nodes.name_zh: Hall 效应与 Hall 电压
nodes.description: Magnetic force deflects charge carriers across a current-carrying material, producing a Hall voltage; VH = BI/(ntq) relates it to flux density, current, carrier density, thickness and carrier charge, and underpins Hall-probe measurements.

nodes.name: Magnetic Fields Due to Currents
nodes.description: The magnetic fields produced by currents in long straight wires, flat coils, and solenoids, with their characteristic field patterns.

nodes.name: Magnetic Flux and Flux Linkage
nodes.description: Magnetic flux through a coil and flux linkage as the product of flux and the number of turns, central to electromagnetic induction.

nodes.name: Faraday's Law
nodes.description: Faraday's law stating that the induced EMF is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage.
nodes.visual_hint: Move a magnet through a coil to induce an EMF (Faraday and Lenz).

nodes.name: Lenz's Law
nodes.description: Lenz's law stating that an induced current opposes the change producing it, a consequence of the conservation of energy.

nodes.name: AC and RMS Values
nodes.description: Alternating current varying sinusoidally with time, and root-mean-square values giving the equivalent steady current for power.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot a sinusoidal AC waveform and its RMS value.

nodes.name: Transformers
nodes.description: Transformers changing alternating voltage using the ratio of turns in the primary and secondary coils, ideally conserving power.
nodes.visual_hint: Transformer diagram relating the turns ratio to the voltage ratio.

nodes.name: Rectification
nodes.description: Rectification converting alternating current to direct current using diodes, in half-wave and full-wave bridge circuits.

nodes.name: Photon Energy
nodes.description: The photon as a quantum of electromagnetic energy, with energy proportional to frequency given by E equals hf.

nodes.name: Photoelectric Effect
nodes.description: The photoelectric effect, the emission of electrons from a metal by incident light above a threshold frequency, evidence for photons.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot photoelectric stopping voltage against frequency.

nodes.name: Wave-Particle Duality
nodes.description: Wave-particle duality, where matter and radiation exhibit both wave and particle behaviour, with the de Broglie wavelength for particles.

nodes.name: Energy Levels and Line Spectra
nodes.description: Discrete electron energy levels in atoms, with line spectra arising from photons emitted or absorbed during transitions between levels.
nodes.visual_hint: Energy-level diagram with photon emission producing line spectra.

nodes.name: Atomic and Nuclear Structure
nodes.description: The nuclear model of the atom with protons and neutrons in a small dense nucleus, described by proton and nucleon numbers.

nodes.name: Isotopes
nodes.description: Isotopes are nuclei of the same element with the same proton number but different numbers of neutrons and therefore different nucleon numbers.

nodes.name: Fundamental Particles and Quarks
nodes.description: Fundamental particles classified as quarks and leptons, with hadrons such as protons and neutrons composed of quarks.

nodes.name: Mass Defect and Binding Energy
nodes.description: Mass defect as the difference between nucleon and nuclear mass, with masses expressed using the unified atomic mass unit u, and binding energy as the equivalent energy holding the nucleus together.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot binding energy per nucleon against nucleon number.

nodes.name: Nuclear Fission and Fusion
nodes.description: Nuclear fission of heavy nuclei and fusion of light nuclei both release energy by moving towards higher binding energy per nucleon; the basis of nuclear power, reactors, and stellar energy.

nodes.name: Radioactive Decay
nodes.description: Spontaneous, random alpha, beta and gamma decay of unstable nuclei, with nucleon number and charge conserved in balanced decay equations. In beta decay, energy is shared by the beta particle, (anti)neutrino and recoiling nucleus, producing a continuous beta-energy spectrum.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot exponential radioactive decay with a slider for half-life.

nodes.name: Half-Life
nodes.description: Half-life as the average time for half the nuclei in a sample to decay, related to the decay constant in exponential decay.

nodes.name: Piezoelectric Transducers
nodes.description: Piezoelectric crystals deform in an applied electric field and generate a potential difference when stressed, allowing transducers to produce and detect pulses of ultrasound.

nodes.name: Acoustic Impedance and Reflection
nodes.description: Acoustic impedance Z = ρc characterises a medium; the intensity reflection coefficient at a normal boundary is determined by the difference and sum of the two media's acoustic impedances.

nodes.name: Ultrasound Imaging and Attenuation
nodes.description: Reflected ultrasound pulses from tissue boundaries provide depth and structural information, while intensity attenuates through matter according to I = I0e^(-μx).

nodes.name: X-ray Production
nodes.description: Electrons accelerated through a potential difference strike a metal target to produce X-rays, with the maximum photon energy and minimum wavelength determined by the electron energy.

nodes.name: X-ray Imaging and Attenuation
nodes.description: X-ray images use differences in tissue attenuation, sometimes enhanced with contrast media; transmitted intensity follows I = I0e^(-μx).

nodes.name: Computed Tomography
nodes.description: Computed tomography reconstructs a two-dimensional image of a slice from many X-ray projections taken at different angles, and combines axial slices to form a three-dimensional image.

nodes.name: Particle-Antiparticle Annihilation
nodes.description: A particle and its antiparticle can annihilate, conserving energy and momentum; electron-positron annihilation at rest produces two equal-energy photons travelling in opposite directions.

nodes.name: Radioactive Tracers and PET
nodes.description: A radioactive tracer is selected for uptake by target tissue; in PET, a positron-emitting tracer and coincidence detection of annihilation photons are used to reconstruct tracer-concentration images.

nodes.name: Luminosity and Radiant Flux Intensity
nodes.description: Luminosity as the total power radiated by a star and radiant flux intensity as the power received per unit area at a distance.

nodes.name: Standard Candles
nodes.description: Standard candles as objects of known luminosity used to determine astronomical distances from their observed brightness.

nodes.name: Stellar Radii
nodes.description: Estimating stellar radii by combining luminosity with surface temperature using the Stefan-Boltzmann law and Wien's law.

nodes.name: Hubble's Law and the Big Bang
nodes.description: Hubble's law relating a galaxy's recession speed to its distance, providing evidence for an expanding universe and the Big Bang.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot recession speed against distance (Hubble's law).
